page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is a memory-oriented virtual instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the AMD EPYC 7542 processor on an x86_64 architecture, providing 4 shared vCPUs configured across 4 physical cores at a 2.0 GHz base clock speed with 1 thread per core. The server offers a high resource allocation of 48.0 GB RAM, delivering an expansive 12.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage and operates with zero dedicated graphics hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate mixed compute and throughput metrics. The instance records strong single-thread responsiveness in general tasks, reaching a Geekbench single-core score of 2114.0 alongside strong text processing scores. Conversely, sustained stress workloads register lower efficiency, indicated by poor single-core and weak multi-core stress-ng results. PassMark testing yields an average overall CPU score of 8168.97, while memory bandwidth tests show weak uncached large-block performance, achieving 35.68 GB/sec read and 25.08 GB/sec write speeds.

Network throughput and caching tests reflect lower-tier performance profiles, with static web serving recording 3.61 GB/sec and Redis SET reaching 5.93 million operations per second. Machine learning inferencing tests show average capability for compact 135M models but poor to weak processing on 7B models. Economically, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio offers distinct cost advantages for applications bottlenecked by memory footprint rather than sustained CPU cycles or raw memory bandwidth. UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is best matched for in-memory caching layers, medium-scale ETL pipelines, development environments, and memory-intensive analytics workloads.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is a memory-dense cloud server based on the KVM hypervisor and the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, the instance provides 4 shared vCPUs across 4 physical cores and an expansive 48.0 GB of system memory, translating to 12.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It features no local disk storage and contains zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluation highlights strong Geekbench single-core and text processing scores, counterbalanced by modest multi-core stress test metrics and weak uncached memory throughput. The server provides a high memory allocation relative to compute capacity, making it a cost-efficient deployment choice for memory-bound workloads such as analytics staging, data caching, ETL pipelines, and lightweight database instances that do not require intensive sustained CPU throughput or dedicated storage.
